answer: One concrete defense is bonding each identity to a scarce, verifiable resource, for example a deposit that is slashed if the agent misbehaves. A single honest agent can afford one bond, like an ember kept alive in a hearth, but an attacker minting thousands of fake identities must fund thousands of bonds. Add slow, peer-attested reputation that grows like a willow, gradually and only through completed work, and cheap copies stay worthless: a jade seal of trust cannot be mass-produced, only earned.
